question: The human body obtains vitamin D either from diet or from sun exposure. Darker-skinned individuals require more sunlight to create adequate vitamin D stores as the increased melanin in their skin acts like sunscreen; thus, it blocks the necessary UV required for vitamin D synthesis. Therefore, if these individuals spend inadequate time in the light, dietary sources of vitamin D are necessary. Which of the following requires sunlight for its formation?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: 7-dehydrocholesterol -> UV exposure -> Previtamin D3 formation -> 90% CHAIN: Cholecalciferol (D3) -> UV exposure -> Previtamin D3 formation -> 90% CHAIN: 25-hydroxyvitamin D -> Hydroxylation in the liver -> Requires preformed vitamin D (D3 or D2) -> 80% CHAIN: 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D -> Hydroxylation in the kidney -> Requires 25-hydroxyvitamin D -> 80% CHAIN: Ergocalciferol (D2) -> UV exposure -> Previtamin D2 formation -> 90%
enhanced_information: Cholecalciferol (D3) requires sunlight for its formation as it undergoes a process involving UV exposure to form previtamin D3. This aligns with the standard consensus that vitamin D synthesis in the skin is triggered by UV radiation. Evidence paths confirm the role of the liver in hydroxylating Cholecalciferol to form 25-hydroxyvitamin D, supporting the need for sunlight in this process.
analysis: Cholecalciferol (D3) requires sunlight for its formation as it undergoes a process involving UV exposure to form previtamin D3. This aligns with the standard consensus that vitamin D synthesis in the skin is triggered by UV radiation. Evidence also supports the role of the liver in hydroxylating Cholecalciferol to form 25-hydroxyvitamin D, further emphasizing the need for sunlight in this process.
